system.name: polygents
system.purpose: A thin, model-agnostic host that lets any model interpret an artifact onto a declared mandate, and lets engines — never the model — return the verdict, with a witness.

sources.note: read at 452588f; status fields record what exists there today

layers.label: L0 · mandate and ledger
layers.note: The only state. Plain files in the customer's repository.

layers.label: L3 · host loop
layers.note: A polyflow workflow, certified before it may run.

layers.label: L2 · interpreters
layers.note: One adapter per provider. Narrow on purpose.

layers.label: L1 · engines
layers.note: Split by licence rather than by convenience.

boundaries.label: Customer's machine
boundaries.claim: Runs with no account and no network; the customer's model source never leaves it

boundaries.label: Oracle service
boundaries.claim: An AWS image the customer never receives; polysim and polyworld are never distributed in any form

components.name: MCP server
components.responsibility: Exposes the polygent to an agent as four tools and returns refusals as ordinary replies rather than protocol errors.
notes: Primary surface: it is what an expert installs in a minute.

components.name: polygent CLI
components.responsibility: Runs a check from a terminal and prints findings first, ending with what the run did not establish.

components.name: CI check run
components.responsibility: Wraps the same core for teams that want a polygent in a pipeline.

components.name: Mandate
components.responsibility: Declares the scope, engines, checks and vocabulary a polygent is answerable for, and is content-hashed into run identity.

components.name: Host loop
components.responsibility: Sequences interpretation, checks and sealing, and makes the doctrine executable as effect invariants.
notes: Itself a checked agent: the workflow is admitted by Library.certify before it can run.

components.name: Reasoning shell
components.responsibility: Maps an artifact onto the mandate's vocabulary and produces an interpretation, never a verdict.
notes: Asked n times independently, and never shown a prior verdict, so agreement means something.

components.name: Model providers
components.responsibility: Answer one narrow call: text in, text out, with the customer's own key.

components.name: Local checks
components.responsibility: Judge the agreed interpretation for coverage, model-code divergence, units and infeasibility.

components.name: Public engines
components.responsibility: Provide the checked primitives the local tier runs on, pinned into the package and resolved by directory probe.
notes: polygraph and polyflow resolve today; polycheck and polyvers are named by the design but not yet bound.

components.name: Solver sandbox
components.responsibility: Runs the customer's solver with the network denied by the kernel so nothing can reach a licence server or a warehouse.
notes: The filesystem hook is a smoke detector, not a vault, and the source says so.

components.name: Customer model source
components.responsibility: Holds the model and solver code the customer is often contractually forbidden to send anywhere.

components.name: Ledger
components.responsibility: Records what happened in order, as the authority, and quarantines rather than repairs when the chain breaks.

components.name: Oracle client
components.responsibility: Builds the only request that leaves the machine, from an explicit allowlist copied by name.
notes: A boundary test puts a canary in a fixture and asserts it never appears in a request.

components.name: Oracle service
components.responsibility: Runs plan replay and robustness on private engines and returns a witness and a digest.

components.name: Entitlement + registry
components.responsibility: Checks entitlement at the boundary and records precision as digests and counts, never customer rows.

components.name: World store
components.responsibility: Holds the generated worlds a plan is replayed against, pinned by worldVersion.

facts.because: so a verdict is a function of the mapping rather than of the model that produced it
a run is a sealed verdict naming what it monitored, or a refusal naming why; there is no third outcome

facts.claim: Disagreement is a note, never a finding
facts.because: items the interpretations did not agree on are excluded from checks and disclosed

facts.claim: The model source never leaves the machine
facts.because: the request body is an explicit allowlist copied by name, asserted by a canary test

facts.claim: The private engines are never distributed
facts.because: polysim and polyworld exist only inside the oracle image, in no form at all

facts.claim: The ledger is the authority and lives in your repository
facts.because: there is no polygents database; a broken chain quarantines rather than repairs

facts.claim: The local tier runs with no account, no key and no network
facts.because: that half is permanent and free, not a trial

facts.claim: A hosted verdict is the one execution you take on our word
facts.because: the customer verifies the returned digest but cannot re-execute it, so it is disclosed on every hosted finding rather than buried

facts.claim: A network failure is a refusal, not a crash
facts.because: the run still seals with whatever the local checks found

questions.title: One core, three doors
questions.ask: How does work enter the system, and where does a verdict actually come from?
questions.answer: Three surfaces hand the same core an artifact and a mandate. The loop interprets with a model, judges with engines, and seals the result. No surface decides anything; it renders what the ledger already says.
questions.omits: The engine boundary and everything hosted. That is its own question.

questions.title: What crosses the engine boundary
questions.ask: What leaves the customer's machine, and what can never leave it?
questions.answer: One request crosses, built from an allowlist: solution values, a world version and an account key. The brief, the model and the solver source stay on the local side, and the private engines stay on ours.
questions.omits: The surfaces, and how the interpretation was produced.

questions.title: Where the model is allowed to speak
questions.ask: If a model cannot be trusted with a verdict, what is it trusted with?
questions.answer: It is trusted to map an artifact onto a declared vocabulary, n times, independently, with no knowledge of prior verdicts. A vote decides what is agreed; anything disputed is excluded and disclosed.
questions.omits: Which specific checks run, and everything across the boundary.

questions.title: Why the verdict is worth anything
questions.ask: What makes a finding evidence rather than an opinion?
questions.answer: Every finding carries a witness from an engine, and every run is appended to a hash-chained ledger in the customer's own repository. Breaking the chain quarantines the run rather than repairing it.
questions.omits: The hosted engines, whose witness arrives across the boundary.
